c1-m1.summary: The user is seeking advice on a hobby they've recently started.
c1-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hi, I'm looking for some advice on a hobby I've recently taken up. I'm not sure if you'll be able to help me, but I thought I'd give it a shot.
Assistant: Of course, I'd be happy to help. What's the hobby you've taken up?
User: Well, I've always been interested in art and design, and I've started experimenting with different materials and techniques.
Assistant: That sounds fascinating. What kind of materials and techniques are you working with?
User: I've been playing around with paints, inks, and dyes. I love the way different colors interact with each other.
Assistant: Color theory is a vast and interesting topic. Are you looking to create something specific, or just exploring the possibilities of different colors?
User: I think I'm just exploring for now. I've always been drawn to vibrant colors and patterns, and I'm trying to learn more about how to create them.
Assistant: Well, there's definitely a lot to learn about color and pigment. Have you considered looking into the chemistry behind different pigments?
User: Actually, I've been reading a bit about that. It's really interesting to learn about how different pigments are created and how they interact with light.
Assistant: Absolutely. Pigments can be really complex, and understanding the chemistry behind them can help you create some amazing effects.
User: Yeah, I've been noticing that. I've met someone who's really into pigments, and they've been teaching me a lot about the different types and how to use them.
Assistant: That sounds like a great resource. What's this person's background with pigments?
User: Well, this person is a pigment enthusiast. They have an incredible collection of pigments from all around the world, and they're always experimenting with new ways to use them.
Assistant: Wow, that sounds amazing. I can imagine you're learning a lot from them. What's the most interesting thing you've learned from this person so far?
User: I think it's the way they combine different pigments to create these incredible, unique colors. They have a real eye for how colors work together.
Assistant: That's a great skill to have. Combining pigments can be a real art form. Do you think you'll continue to work with this person and learn more about pigments?
User: Definitely. I feel like I've only scratched the surface of what's possible with pigments, and I'm excited to see where this hobby takes me.
Assistant: Well, it sounds like you're off to a great start. Keep experimenting and learning, and I'm sure you'll create some amazing things.
User: Hi, I'm looking for some advice on how to manage hand pain. I've been experiencing some discomfort lately.
Assistant: Sorry to hear that. Can you tell me a bit more about what's been going on? What kind of activities trigger the pain?
User: Well, I've just noticed it when I'm doing everyday tasks. Nothing too specific. I'm just wondering if there are any general tips for reducing hand strain.
Assistant: That's a good question. One thing that can help is taking regular breaks to stretch your hands and wrists. It's also a good idea to maintain good posture and avoid bending or twisting your wrists in awkward ways.
User: That makes sense. I'll try to be more mindful of that. But what if the pain is more persistent? Are there any specific exercises or treatments that can help?
Assistant: Yes, there are several exercises you can do to help strengthen your hand and wrist muscles, which can help alleviate pain. For example, you can try squeezing a rubber ball or doing some simple finger stretches. As for treatments, it really depends on the underlying cause of the pain. Have you talked to a doctor about what might be causing your hand pain?
User: Not yet. I was hoping to get some idea of what might be going on before I make an appointment. But I think I might have an idea of what's causing it. I've been doing a lot of activities that involve holding small objects for extended periods.
Assistant: That could definitely be a contributing factor. Holding small objects can put a lot of strain on your hands, especially if you're doing it for a long time. Can you tell me more about what specifically you've been doing that involves holding small objects?
User: Well... I think I might have a bit of a confession to make. I've been dealing with chronic tendinitis in my dominant hand, and it's been making it really painful to hold small objects for extended periods.
Assistant: Ah, I see. That can be a challenging condition to manage. Tendinitis can cause a lot of pain and stiffness, especially when you're doing activities that involve gripping or twisting. Have you tried any treatments or therapies specifically for tendinitis?
User: Not yet. I've just been trying to manage the pain on my own, but it's getting to the point where I need to do something more. Do you have any recommendations for treatments or therapies that might help?
Assistant: Yes, there are several options you could consider. Physical therapy can be very helpful in managing tendinitis, as can corticosteroid injections or pain relievers. In some cases, surgery may even be an option. It's also a good idea to talk to a doctor or a physical therapist about ways to modify your activities to reduce strain on your hand.
User: That's really helpful to know. I think I'll make an appointment with my doctor to discuss some of those options. Do you have any advice on how to manage the pain in the meantime?
Assistant: One thing that might help is using a splint or a brace to support your hand and wrist. This can help reduce strain and alleviate some of the pain. You could also try using heat or cold packs to help reduce inflammation and ease pain. And don't forget to take regular breaks to rest your hand and stretch your fingers and wrist.

Assistant: Ah, an art studio! That sounds like a fun project. I'd be happy to help. One thing to consider is investing in multi-functional furniture, like a storage ottoman or a desk with built-in shelves. What kind of art do you create, by the way?
User: I'm a painter, mostly working with acrylics and experimenting with different pigment combinations. I love the process of discovering new colors and textures.
Assistant: That sounds amazing! I've always been fascinated by the world of color theory. Do you have a favorite piece you've created, or one that you're particularly proud of?
User: Actually, I've been feeling a bit stuck lately. I haven't had as much time to devote to my art as I'd like, and I'm worried I'm losing my momentum. Do you think it's possible to maintain a creative practice while balancing other responsibilities?
Assistant: Absolutely! Many artists have to juggle multiple commitments. One strategy is to schedule dedicated time for your art, even if it's just a few hours a week. What's been taking up most of your time lately?
User: Well, I started working from home a few months ago, and it's been a big adjustment. I'm still figuring out how to separate my work and personal life.
Assistant: That can be tough. It's easy to get sucked into work mode 24/7 when your office is also your living space. Have you considered setting up a dedicated workspace for your job, and keeping your art studio separate?
User: That's a great idea. I think I need to establish some clearer boundaries. Since I started working from home, I've had less time to experiment with new pigment combinations in my art studio. It's like my creative well is drying up!
Assistant: I see. It sounds like you're feeling a bit drained. Let's brainstorm some ways to get your creative juices flowing again. What if you set aside one day a week to focus solely on your art? You could try a new technique, or work on a small project to get your momentum back.
User: That sounds doable. I like the idea of having a dedicated art day. Do you have any suggestions for how to make the most of that time?
Assistant: One approach is to start with a warm-up exercise, like doing some quick sketches or playing with color palettes. Then, you could move on to a more focused project. Remember, the goal is to have fun and reignite your passion for art, not to create a masterpiece in one day!
User: Ha! I need to remind myself of that. I get so caught up in trying to produce something perfect. Thanks for the advice – I feel like I have a plan now.
Assistant: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to help. Don't be too hard on yourself, and remember to enjoy the process. Good luck with your art, and I hope you have a blast rediscovering your creative spark!
User: Hey, I was just thinking about art and how some paintings can be really striking with just a few colors. What do you think makes a piece of art truly memorable?
Assistant: That's a great question! I think what makes art memorable is the way it evokes emotions and sparks imagination. Colors, composition, and the story behind the artwork all play a role in making it unforgettable. Some of the most iconic paintings in history, like the Mona Lisa, use a surprisingly limited color palette to convey a sense of mystery and intrigue.
User: That's really interesting. I never thought about it that way. I guess sometimes simplicity can be just as powerful as complexity.
Assistant: Exactly! Less can often be more, especially when it comes to art. The strategic use of empty space, subtle color choices, and delicate brushstrokes can create a sense of depth and nuance that might get lost in a busier piece.
User: I see what you mean. It's like how some songs can be really catchy with just a simple melody and lyrics.
Assistant: Music is a great analogy! A simple, haunting melody can be just as impactful as a grand symphony. It's all about finding the right balance and using the elements you have to create a lasting impression.
User: Yeah, I think that's true. But what about when things get too simple? Like, have you ever seen a painting that's just one color?
Assistant: Ah, you're talking about monochromatic art! Yes, those can be really striking, but also a bit... dull, depending on the context. I mean, imagine a painting that's just a single shade of gray – it might be a bit too minimalist, even for the most avant-garde art lovers!
User: (laughs) Exactly! That's actually kind of what my life feels like right now. My daily routine has become monotonous, much like a painting with only one shade of gray.
Assistant: Ah, I see what you did there! You cleverly segued from art to life. But seriously, it sounds like you're feeling a bit stuck. Would you like to talk about what's going on and maybe we can brainstorm some ways to add a bit more color to your daily routine?
User: Yeah, that would be great. I just feel like I'm doing the same things every day, and it's getting really old. Wake up, go to work, come home, watch TV, go to bed... it's like I'm just going through the motions.
Assistant: It sounds like you're feeling a bit like you're in a rut. One thing that might help is to shake up your routine by trying something new. It could be as simple as taking a different route to work, trying a new restaurant, or joining a club or group that aligns with your interests. What are some things you've always wanted to try but never had the chance?
User: Hmm, that's a good question. I've always wanted to learn how to play the guitar, but I never seem to have the time.
Assistant: Well, why not start small? You could try dedicating just 10-15 minutes a day to practicing, and see where it takes you. There are plenty of online resources and tutorials that can help you get started. Plus, it's a great way to express yourself creatively and add a bit of excitement to your daily routine.
User: That sounds like a great idea. I think I'll give it a shot. Thanks for the advice!
Assistant: No problem, happy to help! And remember, it's all about adding a bit of color to your life, one small step at a time.

User: Vincent van Gogh, 'Field with Irises near Arles' (F409), 1888, Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam (Vincent van Gogh Foundation).
The colors of 'Field with Irises near Arles', painted by Van Gogh in Arles in 1888, have changed considerably. To get an idea of how this painting, as well as other works by Van Gogh, looked shortly after their production, the Revigo (Re-assessing Vincent van Gogh’s colors) research project was initiated. The aim of this project was to digitally visualize the original colors of paintings and drawings by Vincent van Gogh, using scientific methods backed by expert judgement where required.
We adopted an experimental art technological approach and physically reconstructed Van Gogh’s full palette of oil paints, closely matching those he used to paint Field with Irises near Arles. Sixteen different paints were reconstructed, among which the most light-sensitive pigments and linseed oil, which is prone to yellowing, were produced according to 19th century practice. The resulting pigments and oils were chemically analyzed and compared to those used by Van Gogh. The ones that resembled his paints the most were used in the paint reconstructions. Other pigments were either obtained from the Cultural Heritage Agency’s collection of historical pigments, or purchased from Kremer Pigmente.
The reconstructed paints were subsequently used to calculate the absorption K and scattering S parameters of the individual paints. Using Kubelka-Munk theory, these optical parameters could in turn be used to determine the color of paint mixtures. We applied this method successfully to digitally visualize the original colors of 'Field with Irises near Arles'. Moreover, the set of optical parameters presented here can similarly beapplied to calculate digital visualizations of other paintings by Van Gogh and his contemporaries.
Authors: Muriel Geldof, Art Ness Proaño Gaibor, Frank Ligterink, (Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands), Ella Hendriks (University of Amsterdam) and Eric Kirchner (Akzo Nobel). User: Please provide step-by-step instructions on how to tie-dye a shirt, including the required materials, recommended dye types and colors, and specific techniques for creating different patterns. Be sure to include detailed photos or diagrams to illustrate each step and provide troubleshooting tips for common mistakes or issues. Additionally, please suggest creative ways to personalize and accessorize tie-dye shirts, such as adding embellishments or combining multiple dye techniques.
Assistant: Step-by-Step Guide to Tie-Dye a Shirt

Materials Required:
- White cotton shirt
- Fabric dye (recommended colors: red, blue, and yellow)
- Rubber bands
- Plastic gloves
- A large plastic sheet or garbage bag
- A plastic container
- Water
- Salt
- A stirring tool

Optional Materials:
- Spray bottle 
- Permanent markers 
- Glitter or sequins 

Step 1: Preparing the Shirt
Wash the cotton shirt before beginning the tie-dye process to remove any dirt, oils, or sizing. This allows the dye to penetrate the fabric better. Next, arrange your shirt by laying it flat on a clean and flat surface.

Step 2: Folding and Tying the Shirt
There are various techniques to tie-dye your shirt. Here are some popular and easy ones:

- Spiral Tie-Dye: This method creates a spiral or bullseye pattern. First, pinch the center of the shirt with your index finger and thumb and twist it like a cinnamon roll. Next, crisscross rubber bands around the shirt starting from the center until the whole shirt is tied up tightly. Make sure to keep the shirt flat while tying and overlap the rubber bands to create multiple sections for dyeing.

- Crumple Tie-Dye: This method creates a random, textured pattern. Simply crumple the shirt into a ball or accordion layers and tie it up with rubber bands as randomly or tightly as you want.

- Stripe Tie-Dye: This method creates a vertical or horizontal stripe effect. Fold the shirt horizontally or vertically and tie rubber bands at equal intervals. You can twist some sections before wrapping the rubber bands for added variations.

Feel free to combine and experiment with these methods to create unique designs.

Step 3: Mixing the Dye
Prepare the dye according to the package instructions in a plastic container. Add water to the dye until it reaches the desired shade (usually adding one teaspoon of dye powder to one cup of hot water). To enhance color saturation, add a tablespoon of salt per cup of dye or use a dye-specific fixative.

Step 4: Applying the Dye
Wear plastic gloves to protect your skin from the dye. You can either dip the shirt in the dye or use a spray bottle to apply the colors to specific sections. Apply the dye generously on each section, making sure to saturate the fabric to the center of the folds. For a more blended effect, add multiple colors to certain sections with a paintbrush or dropper.

Step 5: Setting the Dye
After applying the dye, let the shirt rest on a large plastic sheet or garbage bag to prevent the dye from dripping or staining surfaces. Cover the shirt with another plastic sheet or bag to keep it damp and let it sit for at least six hours, or as directed by the dye package. The longer the shirt sits, the more vibrant the colors will be. 

Step 6: Rinse and Wash
Wearing gloves, rinse the shirt under cold water until the water runs clear. Then, remove the rubber bands and continue rinsing until the water remains clear. You can wash the shirt in the washing machine on a gentle cycle with cool water and mild detergent. Alternatively, you can hand-wash the shirt in the sink with a gentle detergent. Do not dry the shirt until you have washed it thoroughly.

Step 7: Personalize and Accessorize
Once your shirt has dried, you can add some personal touches to it. You can use permanent markers, fabric paints, or even glitter to accentuate the tie-dye design. You can also crop the shirt, add fringe to the hem, or turn it into a tank top. Pair your tie-dye shirt with shorts, jeans, skirts, or accessorize with a denim jacket or statement jewelry.



Troubleshooting Tips:

- If the colors bleed or fade, you may not have added enough dye, salt, or pre-soaked the shirt in soda ash before dyeing.
- If the fabric is not saturated enough, the dye will not soak in evenly, resulting in a faded or blotchy pattern.
- If the rubber bands are too tight, they will prevent the dye from seeping in, creating white or light spots instead of the colored sections.
- If the rubber bands are too loose, they will allow the dye to seep in, creating a muddy or blended result. 

With practice and patience, you can create unique and personalized tie-dye designs that showcase your creativity and style.
User: This guide is really helpful! Could you please recommend some alternative types of fabric dye for tie-dye projects? And also, what are some techniques for adding more intricate patterns to my tie-dye shirts?
Assistant: Absolutely! Alternative Fabric Dyes:
While traditional fabric dyes, like Rit, are commonly used for tie-dye projects, there are some other alternatives you can try:

- Natural Dyes: You can use natural substances like fruits, vegetables, and plants to create natural dyes for your tie-dye projects. For example, avocado pits and skins can create a pink color, while turmeric creates a bright yellow. These natural dyes tend to give a more muted and earthy look, but they are fun to experiment with. - Procion Dye: Procion dyes are fiber reactive dyes that can be used for cotton, silk, and other natural fabrics. They are known for their vibrant colors and are often used for tie-dye, batik, and other dyeing techniques. They require a bit more preparation and time, but the results are stunning. - Acid Dye: Acid dyes are used for protein fibers like wool, silk, and nylon. They are available in a wide range of colors and can be used for tie-dyeing or other dyeing techniques. Intricate Patterns:
For more intricate patterns, you can try some of these techniques:

- Shibori: Shibori is a Japanese tie-dye technique that involves binding, twisting, and folding the fabric to create intricate patterns. It can be used with various types of fabric dyes and is great for creating unique and complex designs. - Ice Dyeing: Ice dyeing involves placing ice on the fabric and sprinkling dye powder on top. As the ice melts, the dye seeps into the fabric, creating a watercolor effect. This technique can create stunning results and is also great for experimenting with multiple colors. - Batik: Batik involves using wax to resist the dye and create intricate designs on the fabric. It involves more preparation and tools compared to the traditional tie-dye techniques but can create intricate and detailed patterns. - Ombre: Ombre involves gradually transitioning the colors from one to another. You can dip your shirt in a dye bath and slowly lift it out over time to create a gradient effect from light to dark or vice versa. These techniques may take some practice and experimentation but can result in beautiful and unique tie-dye designs.
User: This is great! Thanks for the tips. Would it be possible to provide some ideas for DIY tie-dye projects other than shirts, like tote bags or bandanas? And do you have any advice on how to mix colors to achieve different shades?
Assistant: Of course, here are some ideas for DIY tie-dye projects other than shirts:

- Tote Bags: Tie-dying a plain canvas tote bag is a fun and easy DIY project that results in a functional and stylish item. You can create unique patterns using the same techniques as shirt tie-dyeing, and you can even personalize the tote bag with a stencil or iron-on transfer.

- Bandanas: Bandanas offer a versatile canvas for tie-dyeing. They can be transformed into a colorful neckerchief, headband, or face mask. You can create classic spiral patterns, stripes, or experiment with more intricate Shibori patterns.

- Socks: Tie-dyeing socks can add a pop of color to any outfit. You can create colorful gradients or patterns that wrap around the ankle or foot.

- Pillowcases: Adding a tie-dyed pillowcase to your bedding can brighten up your bedroom. You can create a matching set, or experiment with different patterns to create an eclectic look.

When it comes to mixing colors, there are a few techniques you can try to achieve different shades:

- Mixing Primary Colors: You can mix equal parts of the primary colors (red, blue, and yellow) to create secondary colors (orange, green, and purple). You can then mix the secondary colors to create tertiary colors (red-purple, blue-green, etc.).

- Diluting Colors: If you want a lighter shade, you can dilute the color by adding more water. Alternatively, you can add more dye to create a darker shade.

- Overlapping Colors: If you want to achieve a unique shade, you can overlap two or more colors on the fabric. For example, overlapping red and blue will create a purple hue.

Make sure to test your color mixture on a small piece of fabric before applying it to the entire item, as colors may appear differently based on the type of fabric and dyes used. Have fun experimenting with color combinations to create your own unique tie-dye designs!

Assistant: Step-by-Step Guide to Tie-Dye a Shirt

Materials Required:
- White cotton shirt
- Fabric dye (recommended colors: red, blue, and yellow)
- Rubber bands
- Plastic gloves
- A large plastic sheet or garbage bag
- A plastic container
- Water
- Salt
- A stirring tool

Optional Materials:
- Spray bottle 
- Permanent markers 
- Glitter or sequins 

Step 1: Preparing the Shirt
Wash the cotton shirt before beginning the tie-dye process to remove any dirt, oils, or sizing. This allows the dye to penetrate the fabric better. Next, arrange your shirt by laying it flat on a clean and flat surface.

Step 2: Folding and Tying the Shirt
There are various techniques to tie-dye your shirt. Here are some popular and easy ones:

- Spiral Tie-Dye: This method creates a spiral or bullseye pattern. First, pinch the center of the shirt with your index finger and thumb and twist it like a cinnamon roll. Next, crisscross rubber bands around the shirt starting from the center until the whole shirt is tied up tightly. Make sure to keep the shirt flat while tying and overlap the rubber bands to create multiple sections for dyeing.

- Crumple Tie-Dye: This method creates a random, textured pattern. Simply crumple the shirt into a ball or accordion layers and tie it up with rubber bands as randomly or tightly as you want.

- Stripe Tie-Dye: This method creates a vertical or horizontal stripe effect. Fold the shirt horizontally or vertically and tie rubber bands at equal intervals. You can twist some sections before wrapping the rubber bands for added variations.

Feel free to combine and experiment with these methods to create unique designs.

Step 3: Mixing the Dye
Prepare the dye according to the package instructions in a plastic container. Add water to the dye until it reaches the desired shade (usually adding one teaspoon of dye powder to one cup of hot water). To enhance color saturation, add a tablespoon of salt per cup of dye or use a dye-specific fixative.

Step 4: Applying the Dye
Wear plastic gloves to protect your skin from the dye. You can either dip the shirt in the dye or use a spray bottle to apply the colors to specific sections. Apply the dye generously on each section, making sure to saturate the fabric to the center of the folds. For a more blended effect, add multiple colors to certain sections with a paintbrush or dropper.

Step 5: Setting the Dye
After applying the dye, let the shirt rest on a large plastic sheet or garbage bag to prevent the dye from dripping or staining surfaces. Cover the shirt with another plastic sheet or bag to keep it damp and let it sit for at least six hours, or as directed by the dye package. The longer the shirt sits, the more vibrant the colors will be. 

Step 6: Rinse and Wash
Wearing gloves, rinse the shirt under cold water until the water runs clear. Then, remove the rubber bands and continue rinsing until the water remains clear. You can wash the shirt in the washing machine on a gentle cycle with cool water and mild detergent. Alternatively, you can hand-wash the shirt in the sink with a gentle detergent. Do not dry the shirt until you have washed it thoroughly.

Step 7: Personalize and Accessorize
Once your shirt has dried, you can add some personal touches to it. You can use permanent markers, fabric paints, or even glitter to accentuate the tie-dye design. You can also crop the shirt, add fringe to the hem, or turn it into a tank top. Pair your tie-dye shirt with shorts, jeans, skirts, or accessorize with a denim jacket or statement jewelry.



Troubleshooting Tips:

- If the colors bleed or fade, you may not have added enough dye, salt, or pre-soaked the shirt in soda ash before dyeing.
- If the fabric is not saturated enough, the dye will not soak in evenly, resulting in a faded or blotchy pattern.
- If the rubber bands are too tight, they will prevent the dye from seeping in, creating white or light spots instead of the colored sections.
- If the rubber bands are too loose, they will allow the dye to seep in, creating a muddy or blended result. 

With practice and patience, you can create unique and personalized tie-dye designs that showcase your creativity and style.

The colors of 'Field with Irises near Arles', painted by Van Gogh in Arles in 1888, have changed considerably. To get an idea of how this painting, as well as other works by Van Gogh, looked shortly after their production, the Revigo (Re-assessing Vincent van Gogh’s colors) research project was initiated. The aim of this project was to digitally visualize the original colors of paintings and drawings by Vincent van Gogh, using scientific methods backed by expert judgement where required.
We adopted an experimental art technological approach and physically reconstructed Van Gogh’s full palette of oil paints, closely matching those he used to paint Field with Irises near Arles. Sixteen different paints were reconstructed, among which the most light-sensitive pigments and linseed oil, which is prone to yellowing, were produced according to 19th century practice. The resulting pigments and oils were chemically analyzed and compared to those used by Van Gogh. The ones that resembled his paints the most were used in the paint reconstructions. Other pigments were either obtained from the Cultural Heritage Agency’s collection of historical pigments, or purchased from Kremer Pigmente.
The reconstructed paints were subsequently used to calculate the absorption K and scattering S parameters of the individual paints. Using Kubelka-Munk theory, these optical parameters could in turn be used to determine the color of paint mixtures. We applied this method successfully to digitally visualize the original colors of 'Field with Irises near Arles'. Moreover, the set of optical parameters presented here can similarly beapplied to calculate digital visualizations of other paintings by Van Gogh and his contemporaries.

Assistant: Creating your own DIY flower pot is a fun and easy project that anyone can do at home. Follow these step-by-step instructions to create your very own customized flower pot:

Materials you'll need:

- Clay - enough to make a pot of your desired size
- Water
- Rolling pin
- Cutting tool
- Parchment paper
- Small stones or pebbles
- Potting mix
- A plant or flower of your choice

Step 1: Begin by kneading and rolling the clay into a ball. You can choose the size of the ball based on the desired size of your pot. Make sure to remove any air bubbles by kneading the clay.

Step 2: Place the clay on a flat surface covered with parchment paper.

Step 3: Use the rolling pin to flatten out the clay into a circle. Use a cutting tool to trim the edges and create an even circle.

Step 4: Fold the edges of the circle towards the middle to create the sides of your pot. Smooth out the seams between the clay.

Step 5: Using a pointed object, create drainage holes on the bottom of the pot. This will allow the water to escape and prevent waterlogging.

Step 6: Allow the clay to dry for 24-48 hours. If you'd like to add texture or designs to your pot, do so after it has dried slightly but before it dries completely.

Step 7: Once the clay is dry, fill the bottom of the pot with small stones or pebbles. This will help with drainage.

Step 8: Fill the pot with potting mix, leaving some space at the top to plant your flower.

Step 9: Plant your flower or plant of your choice in the pot.

Step 10: Display your beautiful DIY flower pot in your home or garden and enjoy your beautiful plant.

Assistant: Homemade Lip Balm Tutorial

Lip balm is a must-have item for anyone looking to keep their lips soft and hydrated throughout the day. Creating your own lip balm is easy and cheaper than purchasing it at a store. Here's a step-by-step tutorial on how to make your own homemade lip balm using natural ingredients such as beeswax, coconut oil, and essential oils.

Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup beeswax pellets
- 1/4 cup coconut oil
- 10-20 drops of essential oil of your choice
- 1 tablespoon honey (optional)

Equipment:
- Double boiler or a heat-safe glass measuring cup and a pot of boiling water
- Measuring cups
- Stirring spoon or spatula
- Lip balm tubes or containers
- Labels 

Step 1: Melt the Beeswax and Coconut Oil 
In a double boiler or a heat-safe glass measuring cup, add the beeswax pellets and coconut oil. Place the double boiler or the glass measuring cup in a pot of boiling water and stir until everything has melted and has combined well.

Step 2: Add Essential Oils 
Once the mixture has melted, add 10-20 drops of the essential oil of your choice. Stir in the oil using a spoon or spatula until it is fully incorporated.

Step 3 (optional): Add Honey 
If you want your lip balm to be a little sweet and moisturizing, add a tablespoon of honey while the mixture is still warm. Stir until the honey has melted and mixed well with the other ingredients.

Step 4: Pour into Containers 
Carefully pour the mixture into your lip balm tubs or containers. Make sure to do it slowly to avoid any air bubbles. Fill the containers until they are almost full, leaving a small space at the top for expansion when the lip balm cools and sets.

Step 5: Let it Cool 
Allow the lip balm to cool and set for at least an hour. You can transfer them to the fridge to speed up the process. 

Step 6: Customize the Scent and Flavor 
If you find the scent of your lip balm too weak, add a few more drops of the essential oil of your choice. For stronger flavors, you can add more honey or even cocoa powder to create a chocolatey flavor.

Step 7: Label and Store
Once your lip balm is fully cooled, add your custom labels to the containers. Store them in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. When stored correctly, your lip balm should last for up to six months. 

Tips and Tricks:
- Ensure that the containers you use are airtight and easy to use. You don't want the balm to spill out when you're applying it.
- Local farmer's markets or health stores are excellent sources for natural ingredients like beeswax.
- You can use a microwave to melt the ingredients if you don't have access to a double boiler.
- If you're making lip balms for different people, include their name on the label so they know it was made specifically for them.

Conclusion:
Making your lip balm is easy and a fun way to customize your beauty routine. With natural ingredients like beeswax, coconut oil, and essential oils, you can create perfectly scented and flavored lip balms that will keep your lips moisturized for hours. So go ahead and experiment with this tutorial, and create a lip balm that is uniquely yours!

User: Write a step-by-step guide on how to create your own DIY flower pot.
Assistant: Creating your own DIY flower pot is a fun and easy project that anyone can do at home. Follow these step-by-step instructions to create your very own customized flower pot:

Materials you'll need:

- Clay - enough to make a pot of your desired size
- Water
- Rolling pin
- Cutting tool
- Parchment paper
- Small stones or pebbles
- Potting mix
- A plant or flower of your choice

Step 1: Begin by kneading and rolling the clay into a ball. You can choose the size of the ball based on the desired size of your pot. Make sure to remove any air bubbles by kneading the clay.

Step 2: Place the clay on a flat surface covered with parchment paper.

Step 3: Use the rolling pin to flatten out the clay into a circle. Use a cutting tool to trim the edges and create an even circle.

Step 4: Fold the edges of the circle towards the middle to create the sides of your pot. Smooth out the seams between the clay.

Step 5: Using a pointed object, create drainage holes on the bottom of the pot. This will allow the water to escape and prevent waterlogging.

Step 6: Allow the clay to dry for 24-48 hours. If you'd like to add texture or designs to your pot, do so after it has dried slightly but before it dries completely.

Step 7: Once the clay is dry, fill the bottom of the pot with small stones or pebbles. This will help with drainage.

Step 8: Fill the pot with potting mix, leaving some space at the top to plant your flower.

Step 9: Plant your flower or plant of your choice in the pot.

Step 10: Display your beautiful DIY flower pot in your home or garden and enjoy your beautiful plant.
User: Can you add more information on how to add designs or textures to the clay pot?
Assistant: Sure! Here are some tips for adding designs or textures to your DIY clay pot:

1. Use a texture stamp: You can use a texture stamp or an old mat to add designs or textures to your pot. Press the texture stamp onto the clay surface or roll the clay over the mat to transfer the design. 2. Use a toothbrush: A toothbrush can be used to create a stippled, speckled or dry-brush effect on the surface of the pot. Dip the toothbrush in a different color of clay slip or paint and then flick it onto the pot’s surface. 3. Use carving tools: You can use carving tools to create intricate designs or patterns on the surface of the pot. You can draw the design onto the pot first or freehand it. Be careful not to carve too deeply, as this can cause the pot to crack or weaken. 4. Use objects around the house: Look for objects around your house, such as leaves, shells, or lace, to press into the surface of the pot or create patterns. You can also use disposable objects like bubble wrap or Styrofoam to stamp designs onto the pot's surface. 5. Use slip: If you want to add a design in a different color to your pot’s surface, you can mix your clay with a different color and apply it onto the surface. Then use a tool like a paintbrush or wooden stick to create or etch a design. You can also use slip to create a pattern by brushing it onto the pot’s surface and then scraping it off to expose the clay underneath. Remember, adding designs and textures to your clay pot is only limited by your creativity! Have fun and experiment with different techniques to make a unique and beautiful pot.
User: Thanks for the tips on how to add designs and textures to the clay pot! Can you elaborate on how to use slip and what materials or colors work best for it?
Assistant: Definitely! Slip is a liquid clay that can be used to create designs on the surface of your clay pot. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to use slip:

Materials you'll need:

- Clay (same as the one you used for your pot)
- Water
- Pigment or underglaze (optional)
- Paintbrush or pipette
- Clay tools

Step 1: Mix a small amount of clay with water to create a creamy consistency. You want the slip to be thick enough to sit on top of the pot's surface but not so thick that it is clumpy.

Step 2: If you want to add color to your slip, you can mix it with pigment or underglaze. Mix thoroughly until you reach the desired color.

Step 3: Use a paintbrush or a pipette to apply the slip onto the surface of the pot. You can apply the slip freehand, use a stencil or trace around a shaped object.

Step 4: Once you have applied the slip to the surface, use a clay tool to create a design or pattern on top of the slip. You can use a wooden stick, a fork, a comb, or even your fingers to create lines, swirls or dabs.

Step 5: Allow the slip to dry for several hours or overnight. Once it is dry, you can add another layer of slip if you want a more intense color or texture.

Step 6: Fire your pot according to the instructions on your clay package.

When using slip, it's always best to test it on a small piece of clay first to see if the color and texture are to your liking. For the color pigments, oxides work best as they will not burn out during firing. Underglaze colors can also be used but may burn out depending on the firing temperature. 

Now that you have a step-by-step guide on how to use slip you can create your own customized designs and patterns on your DIY clay pot!
User: Please write a step-by-step tutorial on how to create homemade lip balm using natural ingredients such as beeswax, coconut oil, and essential oils. Include tips on how to customize the scent and flavor, as well as information on sourcing ingredients and storing the finished product. Please use clear, concise language and provide visual aids (such as photos or diagrams) where appropriate to make the tutorial easy to follow for beginners.
Assistant: Homemade Lip Balm Tutorial

Lip balm is a must-have item for anyone looking to keep their lips soft and hydrated throughout the day. Creating your own lip balm is easy and cheaper than purchasing it at a store. Here's a step-by-step tutorial on how to make your own homemade lip balm using natural ingredients such as beeswax, coconut oil, and essential oils.

Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup beeswax pellets
- 1/4 cup coconut oil
- 10-20 drops of essential oil of your choice
- 1 tablespoon honey (optional)

Equipment:
- Double boiler or a heat-safe glass measuring cup and a pot of boiling water
- Measuring cups
- Stirring spoon or spatula
- Lip balm tubes or containers
- Labels 

Step 1: Melt the Beeswax and Coconut Oil 
In a double boiler or a heat-safe glass measuring cup, add the beeswax pellets and coconut oil. Place the double boiler or the glass measuring cup in a pot of boiling water and stir until everything has melted and has combined well.

Step 2: Add Essential Oils 
Once the mixture has melted, add 10-20 drops of the essential oil of your choice. Stir in the oil using a spoon or spatula until it is fully incorporated.

Step 3 (optional): Add Honey 
If you want your lip balm to be a little sweet and moisturizing, add a tablespoon of honey while the mixture is still warm. Stir until the honey has melted and mixed well with the other ingredients.

Step 4: Pour into Containers 
Carefully pour the mixture into your lip balm tubs or containers. Make sure to do it slowly to avoid any air bubbles. Fill the containers until they are almost full, leaving a small space at the top for expansion when the lip balm cools and sets.

Step 5: Let it Cool 
Allow the lip balm to cool and set for at least an hour. You can transfer them to the fridge to speed up the process. 

Step 6: Customize the Scent and Flavor 
If you find the scent of your lip balm too weak, add a few more drops of the essential oil of your choice. For stronger flavors, you can add more honey or even cocoa powder to create a chocolatey flavor.

Step 7: Label and Store
Once your lip balm is fully cooled, add your custom labels to the containers. Store them in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. When stored correctly, your lip balm should last for up to six months. 

Tips and Tricks:
- Ensure that the containers you use are airtight and easy to use. You don't want the balm to spill out when you're applying it.
- Local farmer's markets or health stores are excellent sources for natural ingredients like beeswax.
- You can use a microwave to melt the ingredients if you don't have access to a double boiler.
- If you're making lip balms for different people, include their name on the label so they know it was made specifically for them.

Conclusion:
Making your lip balm is easy and a fun way to customize your beauty routine. With natural ingredients like beeswax, coconut oil, and essential oils, you can create perfectly scented and flavored lip balms that will keep your lips moisturized for hours. So go ahead and experiment with this tutorial, and create a lip balm that is uniquely yours!
User: This tutorial is really helpful! Is it possible to include some information on how to make tinted lip balm using natural ingredients?
Assistant: Yes, it's definitely possible to make tinted lip balm using natural ingredients. Here's a brief guide on how to create tinted lip balm using beetroot powder:

Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup beeswax pellets
- 1/4 cup coconut oil
- 10-20 drops of essential oil of your choice
- Beetroot powder or other natural pigment (optional)

Equipment:
- Double boiler or a heat-safe glass measuring cup and a pot of boiling water
- Measuring cups
- Stirring spoon or spatula
- Lip balm tubes or containers
- Labels 

Step 1: Melt the Beeswax and Coconut Oil 
Follow Step 1 of the previous tutorial. Step 2: Add Beetroot Powder or Other Natural Pigment
If you want a tinted lip balm, add a small amount, around 1/4 teaspoon, of beetroot powder or other natural pigment of your choice into the melted mixture. Stir the mixture well to distribute the pigment evenly. Step 3: Add Essential Oils and Honey 
Follow Steps 2 and 3 of the previous tutorial. Step 4: Pour into Containers 
Follow Step 4 of the previous tutorial. Step 5: Let it Cool 
Follow Step 5 of the previous tutorial. Step 6: Adjust the Tint 
If you want a stronger tint, you can add more beetroot powder or pigments until you reach the desired shade. Just be cautious not to add too much, or you might end up with a lipstick rather than a lip balm. Step 7: Label and Store 
Follow Step 7 of the previous tutorial. Tips and Tricks:
- If you don't have beetroot powder, you can also use other natural pigments like hibiscus powder, annatto powder, or cocoa powder. - Always start with a small amount of pigment and add more if necessary. - You can customize the shade by mixing different pigments together. - Pigments can stain, so if you're not using gloves, be prepared to have tinted fingers. Conclusion:
Tinted lip balm is an excellent alternative to traditional lipstick. Not only does it provide a hint of color, but it also nourishes and hydrates your lips. With this tutorial, you can create your own tinted lip balm using natural ingredients and customize the shade to your liking. Enjoy!
User: Thanks for the tutorial on how to make tinted lip balm! Can you suggest some other natural pigments that I can use in case I can't find beetroot powder?
Assistant: Yes, of course! Here are some natural pigments that you can use instead of beetroot powder:
- Hibiscus powder: Hibiscus flowers have a vibrant red color that can easily be turned into a powder. This natural pigment creates a beautiful, warm red shade.
- Annatto powder: This pigment is extracted from the seeds of the achiote tree and creates a radiant orange-red color.
- Alkanet root powder: This herb has a deep blue-purple color that can add a gorgeous tint to your lip balm.
- Cinnamon powder: This spice can add a warm, brown hue to your lip balm.
- Cocoa powder: As cocoa powder is already brown, adding a touch of it to your lip balm can give it a slight, sweet chocolate smell and natural tint.

These natural pigments can be found at health food stores or online retailers that specialize in natural ingredients. Be sure to always start with a small amount of pigment and add more until you reach the desired shade. Remember to have fun and experiment with different natural pigments to create a lip balm that is unique to you!

- Potting mix

Step 1: Begin by kneading and rolling the clay into a ball. You can choose the size of the ball based on the desired size of your pot. Make sure to remove any air bubbles by kneading the clay.

Step 5: Using a pointed object, create drainage holes on the bottom of the pot. This will allow the water to escape and prevent waterlogging.

Step 6: Allow the clay to dry for 24-48 hours. If you'd like to add texture or designs to your pot, do so after it has dried slightly but before it dries completely.

Step 7: Once the clay is dry, fill the bottom of the pot with small stones or pebbles. This will help with drainage.

Step 8: Fill the pot with potting mix, leaving some space at the top to plant your flower.

Once the mixture has melted, add 10-20 drops of the essential oil of your choice. Stir in the oil using a spoon or spatula until it is fully incorporated.

If you want your lip balm to be a little sweet and moisturizing, add a tablespoon of honey while the mixture is still warm. Stir until the honey has melted and mixed well with the other ingredients.

Carefully pour the mixture into your lip balm tubs or containers. Make sure to do it slowly to avoid any air bubbles. Fill the containers until they are almost full, leaving a small space at the top for expansion when the lip balm cools and sets.

Allow the lip balm to cool and set for at least an hour. You can transfer them to the fridge to speed up the process.

If you find the scent of your lip balm too weak, add a few more drops of the essential oil of your choice. For stronger flavors, you can add more honey or even cocoa powder to create a chocolatey flavor.

c17-m1.summary: The makeup artist Lucia Pieroni wanted to evoke the collection’s inspiration, a ‘bird feather in water’ (I know, kooky, but stay with me), by making up the models to look like they had just emerged from water.
c17-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: There's special-effects hair and makeup for movies—like Benjamin Button prosthetics or Walking Dead zombie gore—and then there's special-effects hair and makeup like the kind I just saw at Issey Miyake.
Makeup artist Lucia Pieroni wanted to evoke the collection's inspiration, a "bird feather in water" (I know, kooky, but stay with me), by making up the models to look like they had just emerged from water. On the eyes she mixed M.A.C. Platinum Pigment with Water Based Mixing Medium to create a molten metal effect on the lids. When the women blinked, it looked like light reflecting off a watery surface. Then, on the skin, Pieroni applied M.A.C. Strobe Cream under foundation and clear lip balm down the center of the face, mimicking the way "water would trickle down after getting out of the pool." And while you wouldn't want to walk out of the house with lip gloss on your nose (even Pieroni said it wasn't such a great idea), on the runway, her reference was completely and beautifully apparent.
For the hair, Eugene Souleiman took his inspiration from a fabric in the collection. "They've created a weave that causes the fabric to bounce up and down," he explained, "so I wanted the hair to have the same springy effect." I watched as he used an unusual technique, and I swear it was like magic: He prepped the hair with Wella Ocean Spritz and tied it into a ponytail, then tied the ponytail into three knots and bound it with black elastic cord. "It allows air to get into the hair, which is what I want," he said. He let the models wait backstage like that for an hour, and then cut the cords. Then all he had to do was brush the tail out, working in sections. And just like he said, the fabric and the hair bounced down the runway in unison.
How did Eugene Souleiman prepare the models' hair for the show and what was his inspiration?
Assistant: Eugene Souleiman prepped the models' hair with Wella Ocean Spritz and tied it into a ponytail, then tied the ponytail into three knots and bound it with black elastic cord to create a "springy effect" inspired by a weave in the Issey Miyake collection that bounces up and down. He let the models wait backstage like that for an hour and then cut the cords, brushing the tail out in sections.
User: Can you give me more details on the makeup look? Maybe a tutorial or a breakdown of the products used?
Assistant: Of course! Here's a breakdown of the makeup look created by Lucia Pieroni at Issey Miyake:

Skin:
- M.A.C. Strobe Cream applied all over the face as a base
- M.A.C. Face and Body Foundation applied on top of the Strobe Cream for a dewy, natural finish

Eyes:
- M.A.C. Platinum Pigment mixed with Water Based Mixing Medium to create a molten metal effect on the lids
- M.A.C. Black Chromaline applied along the lash line for subtle definition
- M.A.C. Clear Lipglass applied to the center of the eyelid for a wet, glossy effect

Lips:
- M.A.C. Clear Lipglass applied down the center of the face to mimic the way water would trickle down after getting out of the pool

To recreate this look at home, start by applying a hydrating primer or moisturizer to prep the skin. Mix a small amount of M.A.C. Platinum Pigment with a few drops of water or a mixing medium, and apply it all over the eyelids using a flat brush. Use a small amount of black liner or eyeshadow to define the lash line, and finish with a coat of mascara. Apply a clear lip gloss or balm to the center of the face for a subtle, watery effect. Finally, blend a lightweight foundation or tinted moisturizer all over the face for a fresh, natural finish.

c31-m1.summary: The user is a salesperson discussing a project with their boss.
c31-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Boss, I wanted to talk to you about the project we discussed yesterday.
Assistant: Sure, what's on your mind?
User: I strongly believe that your proposed approach isn't the best way to handle this situation. I think we should consider an alternative strategy.
Assistant: Okay, what do you suggest we do instead?
User: Well, I think we should focus more on social media marketing rather than traditional advertising. It's a trend that has been successful for many companies in our industry.
Assistant: I see your point, but how do we measure our success with social media marketing?
User: We can use metrics such as engagement rates, click-through rates, and conversion rates to measure our success. We can also analyze the data and adjust our strategy accordingly.
Assistant: That sounds like a reasonable approach. Let's explore this option further and discuss it with the rest of the team.
User: Great, I'm glad we can come to an agreement. On another note, my shoulder has been bothering me lately. I'm planning to get a massage this week to help alleviate the pain.
Assistant: That sounds like a good idea. Don't hesitate to take care of yourself. Speaking of past situations, have you been meeting your sales quotas recently?
User: Yes, I've been exceeding them for the past few months. Thanks for following up. And about a couple of years ago, I understand why I was fired for not meeting my sales quotas. It was a tough lesson to learn, but it taught me to work harder and smarter.
Assistant: I'm glad to hear that you've been doing well with your sales. And yes, it's important to learn from our past mistakes and grow from them. On a lighter note, let's make sure to keep our work and play separate. I don't think I want to try on any more doll clothes.
User: Haha, duly noted, Boss. We'll stick to discussing work from now on.

c35-m1.summary: Laverne Cox has a strong interest in fashion and has designed some of her own clothing pieces in the past.
c35-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: On Wednesday night, Citizens of Humanity hosted an intimate screening at Soho House of two inspirational short films, one directed by Christy Turlington and the other by Roger Ross Williams. "Every Mile, Every Mother," the model-advocate’s documentary, follows her as she and members of her charity, Every Mother Counts, tackle Oregon’s Hood to Coast marathon relay race in order to raise awareness about the distance some young mothers must travel to get access to maternal care. After the film, Turlington graciously answered questions from the audience, which included Dree Hemingway and Karlie Kloss—and agreed to answer a couple of ours.
Your last film told stories of people who are inspiring. Who most inspires you in your personal life?
I view every person I meet as a potential teacher, but it's probably my children who inspire me to continue to do the work that I do for others.
Who is on your list of inspiring people you have yet to meet?
I would love to meet Sonia Sotomayor someday. She seems like a cool lady, and she is a New Yorker.
How did you begin working with Citizens for Humanity?
Last year I was invited to be featured in their “Just Like You” series. They traveled down to Haiti with us to film it, and we started to think of other ways we could collaborate. We talked about doing a short film and because we were planning to run the Hood To Coast relay for Every Mother Counts later in the year we decided that that would be a good experience to film. We have also just launched a product partnership with them for Mother's Day. A percentage of sales from a few of their most popular Maternity Jeans styles will now benefit EMC. We couldn't be happier about the way this relationship has evolved.
Since founding Every Mother Counts, what do you consider your biggest success?
I am so proud of the growth of our small organization over such a short period of time. To think that my birth story has touched so many others already and that what we are doing is inspiring more people to join the effort is just so meaningful to me. I want us to continue to grow to reach many more but I want to do that very carefully. I am not afraid of making mistakes personally but when you work on behalf of others, the stakes are just too high.
What motivates you as an advocate?
I experienced a childbirth-related complication when I became a mom that many women don't survive. I am advocating that every mother have the same chance to survive as I did.
It's almost Mother's Day. How are you celebrating?
I like to think that every day is Mother's Day. Every Mother's Day 800 women die bringing life into the world, and that’s not just on Mothers Day, its every day. But the good news is, 90 percent of these deaths are preventable. That's something we can celebrate. But we need more people to be aware of this so we introduced our Every 2 Minutes campaign, which is designed to educate and engage others to be part of the solution. The campaign provides a lot of great ways that people can take two minutes to take two actions to help raise awareness and spread the word, which is detailed on our site.
Christy Turlington. Photo by BFAnyc.com. Based on the passage above, Who does Turlington consider to be the biggest inspiration in her personal life, and who is on her list of people she would like to meet?
Assistant: Turlington considers her children to be the biggest inspiration in her personal life. She would like to meet Sonia Sotomayor.
User: Could you please provide more details on Every Mother Counts and their mission?
Assistant: Every Mother Counts is a non-profit organization that aims to make pregnancy and childbirth safer for every mother worldwide. The organization was founded by Christy Turlington Burns after experiencing a childbirth-related complication during the delivery of her first child. Every Mother Counts works to increase access to medical care, education, and support for pregnant women and new mothers. The organization advocates for policies and partnerships that support maternal health and provides grants to community-based organizations that work towards improving maternal health outcomes. Every Mother Counts conducts research and raises awareness about the maternal health crisis globally through their campaigns and partnerships.
User: Can you provide more information on Every Mother Counts' Every 2 Minutes campaign and how people can get involved?
Assistant: The Every 2 Minutes campaign by Every Mother Counts is designed to inform and engage people to take action to prevent maternal mortality. The campaign highlights the staggering statistic that every two minutes, a woman dies due to complications related to pregnancy or childbirth. However, the good news is that 90 percent of these deaths can be prevented with access to basic maternal healthcare. 

The campaign encourages people to take two minutes to take two actions to help spread the word and raise awareness about the maternal mortality crisis. People can participate in the following ways:

1. Educate Yourself: Visit the Every 2 Minutes website to learn more about the issue, access resources, and take quizzes to test your knowledge.

2. Take Action: Every 2 Minutes offers a range of actions people can take, including sharing information on social media, sending letters to legislators, and hosting fundraising events.

3. Speak Out: Use social media to share the issue with family and friends, attend events, and talk to people in your community about the importance of investing in maternal healthcare.

4. Support Every Mother Counts: By giving a donation, purchasing products, or hosting fundraising events, people can directly support Every Mother Counts' work to improve maternal health outcomes.

Overall, the Every 2 Minutes campaign is a call to action to encourage people to acknowledge and address the global maternal health crisis.

User: On Wednesday night, Citizens of Humanity hosted an intimate screening at Soho House of two inspirational short films, one directed by Christy Turlington and the other by Roger Ross Williams. "Every Mile, Every Mother," the model-advocate’s documentary, follows her as she and members of her charity, Every Mother Counts, tackle Oregon’s Hood to Coast marathon relay race in order to raise awareness about the distance some young mothers must travel to get access to maternal care. After the film, Turlington graciously answered questions from the audience, which included Dree Hemingway and Karlie Kloss—and agreed to answer a couple of ours.
Your last film told stories of people who are inspiring. Who most inspires you in your personal life?
I view every person I meet as a potential teacher, but it's probably my children who inspire me to continue to do the work that I do for others.
Who is on your list of inspiring people you have yet to meet?
I would love to meet Sonia Sotomayor someday. She seems like a cool lady, and she is a New Yorker.
How did you begin working with Citizens for Humanity?
Last year I was invited to be featured in their “Just Like You” series. They traveled down to Haiti with us to film it, and we started to think of other ways we could collaborate. We talked about doing a short film and because we were planning to run the Hood To Coast relay for Every Mother Counts later in the year we decided that that would be a good experience to film. We have also just launched a product partnership with them for Mother's Day. A percentage of sales from a few of their most popular Maternity Jeans styles will now benefit EMC. We couldn't be happier about the way this relationship has evolved.
Since founding Every Mother Counts, what do you consider your biggest success?
I am so proud of the growth of our small organization over such a short period of time. To think that my birth story has touched so many others already and that what we are doing is inspiring more people to join the effort is just so meaningful to me. I want us to continue to grow to reach many more but I want to do that very carefully. I am not afraid of making mistakes personally but when you work on behalf of others, the stakes are just too high.
What motivates you as an advocate?
I experienced a childbirth-related complication when I became a mom that many women don't survive. I am advocating that every mother have the same chance to survive as I did.
It's almost Mother's Day. How are you celebrating?

But the good news is, 90 percent of these deaths are preventable. That's something we can celebrate. But we need more people to be aware of this so we introduced our Every 2 Minutes campaign, which is designed to educate and engage others to be part of the solution. Passage: He may not know quite when it is, but that has not stopped Cleary’s boxer Lewis Williams dreaming of an appearance at the Commonwealth Games in Australia.
The 18-year-old was last week confirmed as a member of the GB Boxing Podium Potential squad which gives him three months to impress the Great Britain coaches with a view to remaining part of the GB World Class Programme as it targets Tokyo 2020.
However, for Williams, the Gold Coast in 2018 is his primary aim as he looks to unseat 91kg rival and current GB podium boxer Cheavon Clarke.
He added: “I’ve got my foot in the door and now I need to keep going through the ranks. I’ll keep working and keep my feet on the ground and stay focused.
Williams has come through the ranks at Cleary’s, having started out with skills bouts and moved through to box for his country in the World Youth Championships.
However, despite catching the eye of the Great Britain selectors, team training camps in Sheffield will need to be balanced with his education as he prepares to start a mechanical engineering course at Coventry University.
For now though, injuries are furthest from his mind as he plots a path which will eventually see him switching to the pro ranks.
And, having coached him since he stepped into his gym as an 11-year-old Edwin Cleary has no doubt he has got what it takes to reach the very top.
“He’s got a winner’s mentality, dreams big and has determination to match,” said Cleary.
“There will be comparisons I’m sure to the late, great Randy Turpin and if he could match his achievement I for one would be extremely proud.

Finally, provide examples of music videos that have had a significant impact on fashion trends and explain why they were influential.
Assistant: Music videos have played a major role in shaping fashion trends over the years. They serve as a platform for musicians and designers to showcase their talent, creativity, and style. Music video fashion often reflects the prevailing cultural norms and trends of the time, and can be highly influential in shaping popular fashion. 

One way music videos have impacted fashion trends is by introducing new styles and aesthetics to a wide audience. For example, music videos of the 1980s were characterized by bold colors, flashy accessories, and big hair, which inspired a wave of retro-inspired fashion. Similarly, the grunge-inspired fashions of the 1990s were popularized by music videos from bands like Nirvana and Pearl Jam, and these styles continue to be a staple of mainstream fashion today.

Different genres of music have also played a significant role in shaping fashion trends. For example, the punk aesthetic of the 1970s gave rise to a style that was rebellious, edgy, and often minimalistic. Hip hop and rap have also had a major impact on fashion trends, especially when it comes to streetwear and sportswear.

Music video fashion is often characterized by bold, theatrical costumes, accessories, and makeup. These elements are used to create a unique visual image that complements the music and lyrics. Music video fashion can range from the elaborate costumes of Lady Gaga to the minimalist streetwear of A$AP Rocky. 

Some music videos that have had a significant impact on fashion trends include Madonna's "Material Girl" (1985), which inspired a wave of 1950s retro fashion; Michael Jackson's "Thriller" (1983), which popularized red leather jackets and zombie makeup; and Beyoncé's "Formation" (2016), which celebrated black culture and inspired a resurgence of black activism-inspired fashion. 

In conclusion, music videos have had a substantial impact on fashion trends, shaping popular culture and inspiring new styles and aesthetics. The fashion in these videos has influenced the way people dress, and different genres of music have played a significant role in shaping fashion trends. Music video fashion is characterized by bold, theatrical costumes and makeup, and has produced some of the most iconic styles of the past few decades.

Goth fashion is known for its dark, dramatic, and often Victorian-inspired style, characterized by black and white clothing, corsets, lace, and leather. The music videos of the 1980s by bands like The Cure, Siouxsie and the Banshees, and Bauhaus helped popularize the goth look and inspired a dedicated subculture. Similarly, emo fashion emerged in the late 1990s and was characterized by a dark, moody, and angsty style, often featuring skinny jeans, band t-shirts, studded belts, and heavy eyeliner. Emo bands like My Chemical Romance, Fall Out Boy, and Panic! at the Disco helped popularize the emo look with their music videos which showcased unique and edgy fashion styles. Some music videos that showcase unique and innovative fashion styles include:

1. Lady Gaga - "Bad Romance" (2009): This music video features Lady Gaga in various high fashion looks, including a white Alexander McQueen gown and an iconic Alexander McQueen lobster claw shoes. 2. Bjork - "Human Behaviour" (1993): This music video features Bjork in an iconic swan dress designed by Marjan Pejoski, which became one of the most memorable fashion moments in music video history. 3. Missy Elliott - "The Rain (Supa Dupa Fly)" (1997): This music video features Missy Elliott in a futuristic inflatable jumpsuit, which became one of the most iconic fashion moments of the late 1990s. 4. David Bowie - "Life on Mars?" (1973): This music video features David Bowie in an iconic blue suit and platform shoes, which influenced fashion trends in the 1970s and beyond. 5. The White Stripes - "Seven Nation Army" (2003): This music video features The White Stripes in their signature red, white, and black outfits, which have become synonymous with their unique and innovative style. These music videos showcase the ways in which music video fashion can be daring, expressive, and boundary-pushing, and inspire new trends and styles in the fashion world.
User: Are there any trending shoe styles that are both comfortable and fashionable?
Assistant: Yes, there are several shoe styles currently trending that are both comfortable and fashionable, including:

1. Sneakers: Athletic shoes are no longer just for working out. Nowadays, sneakers come in a variety of styles and colors, and can be dressed up or down. Brands like Nike, Adidas, and Puma offer comfortable and stylish options.

2. Loafers: These slip-on shoes are a staple for both men and women. They come in a variety of materials, from leather to suede to velvet, and can be worn with everything from jeans to dresses.

3. Mules: These backless shoes are a popular trend this season, and for good reason. They're easy to slip on, comfortable to wear, and can make any outfit look chic.

4. Block heel sandals: Block heels are both sturdy and stylish, making them perfect for all-day wear. Sandals with a block heel can be dressed up or down, and are a great option for summer.

5. Combat boots: These boots have been around for a while, but they're making a comeback this season. With a chunky sole and lace-up design, they provide both comfort and edge to any outfit.
User: I love sneakers, but I'm looking for something a bit more dressy. Any suggestions?
Assistant: If you're looking for a shoe that's dressier than sneakers, but still comfortable, here are a few options to consider:

1. Flats: Ballet flats are a classic option that can be dressed up or down. Look for ones with a cushioned sole or arch support for extra comfort.

2. Wedges: Wedges provide height without sacrificing comfort. Look for ones with a cork or rubber sole for added cushioning.

3. Pointed-toe heels: A pointed-toe heel can make any outfit look dressier. Look for ones with a lower heel height and a padded footbed for comfort.

4. Block heels: Similar to pointed-toe heels, block heels provide height while being more stable and comfortable to walk in.

5. Mary Jane flats: These shoes have a strap across the top of the foot and a flat or low heel. They're dressy enough for work or events, but still comfortable to wear all day.
User: I really like the idea of wedges, but I'm afraid they might be too difficult to walk in. Do you have any tips for wearing them comfortably?
Assistant: If you're concerned about walking in wedges, here are a few tips that may help:

1. Look for wedges with a lower heel: Wedges come in a variety of heel heights, so look for ones that are a little shorter if you're not used to walking in them. A wedge with a 1-2 inch heel can still give you some height while being easier to walk in.

2. Choose wedges with a stable base: Look for wedges with a wider base, which will provide more stability when you're walking.

3. Opt for wedges with ankle straps: Ankle straps can give added support and help keep the shoe in place while you walk.

4. Practice walking in them: Before wearing your wedges out, practice walking around your house or on a carpeted surface to get used to the feeling of walking in them. This can help you feel more confident when you wear them out.

5. Add cushioning: Some wedges come with a cushioned insole, but if yours don't, you can add cushioning inserts to provide extra comfort and support.

Rather, they are attending martial arts classes because they personally enjoy it. Instilling this form of motivation is very important for keeping your retention rates high.

Third, trust needs to be built between instructors and students to create better bonds.
